description_full: dormakaba Holding AG provides access and security solutions worldwide. It offers door hardware products, including door closers, locks, fittings, emergency exits, and panic hardware; interior glass systems comprising manual sliding, manual single and double action door, fittings for glass assemblies, and horizontal sliding walls; and entrance systems, such as swing operators, automatic sliding doors, sliding door operators, revolving doors, security revolving doors and interlocks, connectivity, sensor barriers and speed gates, and turnstiles. The company also provides mechanical key systems, including cylinder locks with reversible keys, master key systems, planning and maintenance; electronic access and data comprising electronic cylinders, electronic door locks, digital door locks, card readers and peripherals, electromagnetic locks, and time and attendance; lodging systems that include access management systems, electronic hotel locks, digital wallets, and perimeter access; and safe locks under the Axessor Appex Series, Axxesor, Paxos, Cencon, CenconX, Auditcon, LA GARD electronic, Mauer electronic, Mauer mechanical, LA GARD mechanical, X-0 series brands. In addition, it offers access control, accessibility, fire protection, hygiene and infection prevention, mobile access, people flow and security, touch-free access, and automatic door systems solutions. The company serves the airport, healthcare, hospitality, multihousing, datacenters, rail, office, residential, and utilities industries. dormakaba Holding AG was founded in 1862 and is headquartered in Rümlang, Switzerland.

financial_summary: Dormakaba Hldg AG is a mid-cap industrials business with a $3.3B market cap on $3.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 26% against a 7% cost of capital — a 19-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 41%.

The business throws off $192M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.99× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 9.9×.
Shareholder yield is only 1.4%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 31% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sector_headwinds.text: Industrials sector lagging the market significantly, underperforming by 6% over 3 months
Cyclicality and capital intensity — order books turn on a dime, and the heavy fixed cost base that creates the moat also magnifies the downturn.
Supply chain reshoring costs and labour shortages — onshoring mandates raise capex requirements while a shrinking skilled-labour pool inflates operating costs.
Tariff and trade-policy exposure — industrial exporters sit squarely in the crosshairs of protectionist policy, and retaliatory tariffs can close markets without warning.
